title: Development of a Predictive Model for Runway Water Film Depth
content: Water film depth (WFD) on runways is a key factor contributing to aircraft hydroplaning during takeoff and landing. Thus, early measurement or prediction of WFD during raining is critical for reducing aviation occurrences. Most existing WFD prediction models are derived from relevant experiments conducted on road surfaces. However, an accurate prediction of WFD on runways and reduction of hydroplaning risks requires a precise empirical prediction model. This study conducts experiments involving four parameters, rainfall intensity, pavement mean texture depth, drainage length, and transverse slope, to develop a WFD dataset specific to different runway conditions. Multiple linear regression method is employed to establish a model for WFD predictions. The predictability of the proposed National Taiwan University (NTU) model is compared with four existing empirical models using NTU and Gallaway datasets. The results clearly demonstrate the superior accuracy and robustness of the NTU model compared to the other four evaluated models. The NTU model offers a precise and practical predictive formula, making it highly suitable for integration into contaminated runway warning and management systems.
